newsitem.title: INDIA: India council urges phone industry incentives.
newsitem.headline: India council urges phone industry incentives.

text.p: India can have a 100 percent digital telephone service network by 2015 if proper incentives are provided by the government to create an investor-friendly climate, an autonomous body said on Friday.

The Technology Information, Forecasting and Assessment Council (TIFAC), set up by the government to advise the industry and the government, said a coherent regulatory mechanism was needed to boost the quality of India's telecom services.

"Adoption of international standards in telecom equipment production and India's taking part in global deliberations and discussions are also needed for moving towards the target," TIFAC chairman Bishnu Pradhan told Reuters.
Only 65 pecent of India's telecom network is currently digitalised. It is expected to increased to 75 percent by the turn of the century, Pradhan said.

"While the major initiative in realising the 2015 vision for telecommunications will need to come from the government, it is clear that industry, regulators, research and development institutions and users themselves have a crucial role to play, TIFAC said in a statement released at a conference in Delhi.

Industry and government officials said the telecom sector should to be given an infrastructure industry status, the development of which was needed to provide telephone services to anyone at affordable prices.
"It should be our endeavour to integrate telecom industry formally to the infrastruture sector," said A.V. Gokak, secrerary of the Department of Telecommunications.
Industry officials say that India currently has one telephone per 100 people compared to six per 100 in Malaysia and Brazil.
